newsitem.title: UK: BFI climbs back to 1,000; Panamaxes look stronger.
newsitem.headline: BFI climbs back to 1,000; Panamaxes look stronger.

text.p: After precisely one week below 1000 the Baltin Freight Index (BFI) climbed back up to precisely this level on Monday after adding two points from Friday's figure.
In spite of holidays in China, the Pacific was reported by brokers to be looking stronger for Panamaxes, but otherwise the week has started quietly in the freight market.

Some discouraging developments for owners came with the news that two capers, the 1975-built Kleovoulos of Rhodes 123,770 dwt and 1976-built Tahir Kaptan 122,146 dwt, had been rejected for loading iron ore by Brazilian port authorities.

There was also a report from reliable sources that an early 1980's-built small Panamax had gone into lay-up in Greece, believed to be the first vessel to suffer this fate as a result of market conditions in recent times.
GRAIN -
The grain market was flat. Brokers reported difficulty assessing the course of activities by the crucial Chinese interests.

One main house pointed out the availablility of up to half a dozen Chinese-controlled Panamaxes in the Atlantic, but others believed that PRC charterers had fixed Morning Cloud 66,967 dwt delivery Amsterdam mid-October for 2-4.5 months trading in the low $7,000's which might suggest the Chinese were not long on early tonnage.
But on last week's evidence Chinese vessels seem likely to continue to play an active part in the inter-Atlantic grain trades.

Few new grain orders were quoted today but among the larger sizes Cargill have 2.4-3.2m CFT Brazil/Lisbon-Hamburg range for Oct 23/30, probably workable at a little over $11,00, and Transgrain 50,000 meals up river and Brazil/China for Oct 5/20, at ideas $23.50.
Iranian interests quoted 60,000 wheat St Lawrence/Iran for October shipment as well Nopac/Iran for Oct/Nov.

Glencore was still active in handy-size business from the continent, having fixed 20/25,000 barley prompt from Rouen to Cuba at $24.50. Sidmar were said to have covered 20,000 wheat Rouen/west coast Italy on private terms.
Minerals etc -

One broker described the Caper market as "totally lacking in direction". Reported business was negligible although EEC confirmed booking Olivia for 150,000 iron ore PDM/Constanza at $5.60 as a replacement for tonnage rejected by loading authorities.
New Atlantic coal business for Oct loading was quoted by Bocimar with 60,000/10 Bolivar/Liverpool, Glencore 60,000 Mississippi/Liverpool, and Sidmar/Lalemant Hampton Roads/Terneuzen-ent.
Handy-sizes -

The Lakes market remained strong - SCM was forced to pay as much as $9,500 daily for the 1974-built Canadian Forest-relet Maria GL 26,980 dwt delivery prompt continent for a trip via Rostock to the Lakes with steels.
Sealift fixed a multi-purpose tweendeck vessel on private terms from Hamburg to east Africa, and Taxiarhis P 33,000 dwt was fixed on charter party details from U.S. Gulf.
Little was reported in the east except Tamai's fixture of Soarer Bellona 43,509 dwt from Bintang to Japan at $8,200 daily.
Transfield covered cheaply with Legionario 44,541 dwt delivery prompt Sumatra via Australia to China at $7,000 daily.
